subject: Visibility & Ops: Implementation sprint — dashboard routing, tracing hooks & runbook plan
messages:
From: Amelia Stone <amelia@nexushealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-10-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood kickoff — visibility & alerts scope

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering and SRE teams are ready to start the visibility/ops onboarding for Redwood. High-level asks from NexusHealth:

- Dashboards that show per-model latency P95/P99, token cost per-call, and query distribution by route
- Tracing hooks for our microservice that calls Redwood (Java service) — we'd like span examples and minimal instrumentation samples
- Error taxonomy mapping (retries vs. user errors vs. model-quality anomalies) so our oncall knows escalation steps
- Alert routing rules: dev/staging -> PagerDuty dev schedule, prod -> PagerDuty SRE + CS on-call
- A runbook template we can drop into our Confluence for incident playbooks

Our target: pilot rollout to staging by 2029-10-25 and production in early November. Can you send a mutual action plan and what you need from our side (logs, sample traces, IAM roles)?

Best,
Amelia
Amelia Stone
Director, Platform Engineering — NexusHealth

Attachment: nexus-current-infra.pdf (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Stone <amelia@nexushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-10-10T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood kickoff — visibility & alerts scope

Amelia — thanks, this is great and aligns with what I had in mind. Quick reply with next steps and ask list; internal plan to follow.

Ask for NexusHealth before the kickoff:
- Short sample request/response logs (sanitized) with at least 24h of production-like traffic for the staging window
- One representative request payload and the corresponding downstream service logs for tracing examples
- List of service account emails to grant read-only perf telemetry during setup

We will:
- Deliver a dashboard seed (Grafana/Looker) with P95/P99 latency, token-cost per route, and token-distribution by prompt type
- Provide a lightweight tracing hook snippet for Java (OpenTelemetry) plus a short example trace map for your team to import
- Produce an error taxonomy doc mapping common Redwood responses to suggested retry/escalation actions
- Draft a runbook template and proposed alert routing (dev/staging/prod) for your approval

I'll loop in Laura and Marissa to work out staffing and timing. Tentative kickoff call: 2029-10-16 10:00 PT — does that work?

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-implementation-checklist.pdf (stub), runbook-template.md (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-10-10T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: NexusHealth visibility kickoff — roles & prework

Team — quick internal coordination. NexusHealth (Amelia) asked for a staging pilot by 10/25 and prod in early Nov. Key deliverables:

1) Dashboard seed (Grafana):
   - Panels: P95/P99 latency per model, token-cost per call, throughput by route, 24h heatmap of prompt lengths
   - Data sources: Redwood telemetry + NexusHealth request logs (we'll point to their s3/CloudWatch)

2) Tracing hooks:
   - Provide OpenTelemetry Java snippet + example spans showing client->redwood->downstream services
   - Create a small sample trace image (nexushealth-trace-map.png) and instrument guidance (what to attach to spans: route_id, model_version, token_count)

3) Error taxonomy + runbook:
   - Draft taxonomy (client errors, transient infra, model-quality). For each: alert thresholds, suggested mitigations, pager routing, and playbook steps

4) Alert routing and oncall mapping:
   - Dev/staging -> Nexus dev PD schedule
   - Prod -> Nexus SRE PD + Redwood CS on-call (escalate after 15m)

Prework for this week (by 2029-10-13):
- Laura: mock Grafana panels and query templates (use the demo metrics we have).
- Marissa: draft error taxonomy and runbook template; include suggested escalation matrix.
- Sean: prepare Java OTEL snippet and a schematic trace map.

I'll own the kickoff agenda and mutual action plan doc. Laura/Marissa/Sean — if timing works, we'll present the seed dashboard on the kickoff and get Nexus to provide sample logs during the call.

Ben

Ben — 10/16 at 10:00 PT works for us. A couple clarifications before the call:

- We'll share a 48h sample of sanitized logs; can you confirm the exact fields you need (headers, time, request_id, prompt_length, model_label)?
- For tracing, our Java service uses OpenTelemetry already; we mostly need the exact span attributes to add for correlation (so our traces link to Redwood request ids).
- On the PD routing: we can add Redwood CS on-call as an escalation contact, but Nexus legal requires a very short description of what Redwood will see/access (read-only telemetry) — can you provide that text?

Also putting in a request: if you have a short checklist for compliance (what artifacts we need for an audit) that would help our audit team for production rollout.

Thanks — Amelia

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Stone <amelia@nexushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-10-12T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood kickoff — visibility & alerts scope (mutual action plan attached)

Amelia — great, thanks for confirming the 10/16 kickoff. Attached is a short mutual action plan and the compliance artifacts checklist. Highlights in the MAP:

- Pre-kickoff (due 10/13): Nexus provides 48h sanitized logs (fields: timestamp, request_id, route_id, model_label, prompt_length, client_ip(optional), response_status) + list of service accounts
- Kickoff (10/16): Walkthrough of dashboard seed, tracing snippet, initial taxonomy; import sample trace live
- Post-kickoff (10/17-10/24): Integration sprint — Redwood seeds dashboards in Nexus staging, Nexus validates queries and provides feedback
- Staging signoff (target 10/25): Nexus to confirm runbook acceptance and alert routing in PD
- Prod rollout (tentative week of 11/4): Redwood supports a 2-day hypercare window after cutover

Compliance blurb for Nexus legal (to include in their confluence):
"Redwood Inference will have read-only visibility into telemetry related to Redwood API requests for the purposes of onboarding and ongoing support. This includes request/response metadata (timestamps, request_id, route_id, model_version, token counts) and aggregated performance metrics. Redwood will not access customer PII or full prompt text without explicit consent; any sanitized payloads will be pre-approved by Nexus. Access will be scoped to designated service accounts and logged for audit."

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-nexushealth.pdf (stub), compliance-artifact-checklist.pdf (stub)

Next steps: I'll post the MAP to the shared Drive link and send a calendar invite for 10/16 10:00 PT. Laura/Marissa/Sean — please bring the seed items noted in the prework.

Best,
Ben
